Simulate 2D natural convection in a square cavity using the de Vahl Davis benchmark configuration with the solver buoyantBoussinesqPimpleFoam in OpenFOAM.
The domain is a square cavity with side length 0.1 m in both x and y directions.
Discretize the domain with a uniform structured mesh of 100 cells in x and 100 cells in y.
Represent the 2D problem as a 1-cell-thick 3D mesh in the z direction with empty boundary patches on the front and back faces.
Model the fluid as air using constant transport properties at the film temperature of 295 K: rho = 1.177 kg/m3, mu = 1.789e-5 Pa.s, pr = 0.703, and thermal expansion coefficient beta = 1/295 = 3.390e-3 1/K.
Apply the Boussinesq approximation for buoyancy in the momentum equation.
Set the gravitational acceleration vector to g = (0, -9.81, 0) m/s^2.
Set the left wall (x = 0) temperature boundary condition to fixedValue with T = 300 K.
Set the right wall (x = 0.1 m) temperature boundary condition to fixedValue with T = 290 K.
Set the top wall (y = 0.1 m) temperature boundary condition to zeroGradient (adiabatic).
Set the bottom wall (y = 0) temperature boundary condition to zeroGradient (adiabatic).
Set the velocity boundary condition on all four cavity walls to noSlip.
Set the pressure boundary condition on all four cavity walls to zeroGradient.
Configure buoyantBoussinesqPimpleFoam for a transient simulation with endTime = 200 s.
Set the writeInterval to 10 time units (seconds) so results are written every 10 s.
Set the solver convergence tolerance (residual threshold) to 1e-6 for all fields.
Initialize the velocity field to zero (U = 0) throughout the domain.
Initialize the temperature field to a uniform value of 295 K throughout the domain.
Initialize the pressure field (p_rgh) to zero throughout the domain.
